note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Follow principles of Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) in work environment

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A risk matrix scores likelihood and severity from 1 to 5 each, and multiplies them. A hazard is 'likely' (4) and the harm would be 'major' (4). What is the risk score?
After engineering controls are added, a task's risk score is still high. What is the right next step?
options: Start the work, since some controls are now in place
Ask the workers to take extra care and carry on
Lower the score on the form so that the job can start
Add more controls before any of the work starts

questions.stem: Which of these is an engineering control for welding fume?
options: A respirator worn by each welder
A fume extraction arm at the weld
Rotating welders between jobs
A toolbox talk on fume hazards

questions.stem: Which is an example of eliminating the hazard of working at height?
options: Using a harness while welding a sign frame up a pole
Welding the frame on the ground, then lifting it up
Putting a warning sign at the foot of the ladder
Giving the welder a longer ladder to work from

questions.stem: Which is an example of substitution as a control?
options: Fitting a guard to a bench grinder
Wearing chemical gloves when degreasing
Limiting the time spent degreasing parts
Using a water-based degreaser, not a solvent

questions.stem: Which of these is an administrative control?
options: A fixed machine guard on the power guillotine
A fume-rated respirator for each welder
A hot work permit system with a fire watch
Removing a gas line that is no longer used

questions.stem: Why does welding stainless steel need extra care with fume control?
options: Its fume can hold chromium compounds that cause cancer
Stainless steel gives off lead fume when it is welded
Stainless steel throws far more sparks than mild steel
The fume from stainless steel is always easy to see

questions.stem: Why should a welder keep their head out of the fume plume rising from the weld?
options: The plume makes the arc harder to see through the filter
The plume cools the weld and causes cracks
Heat from the plume can crack the helmet's lens
It carries fume straight to the nose and mouth

questions.stem: Why must chlorinated solvent degreasers be kept well away from arc welding?
options: The solvent makes the weld metal too hard
The arc's UV light can turn the vapour into a very toxic gas
The solvent removes the flux from the electrodes
The vapour makes the arc too bright to look at

questions.stem: Before a welder enters a water tank to weld inside it, what must be done?
options: Open the manhole and send the welder in
Give the welder a dust mask and a torch
Wait until the tank has cooled in the evening
Get a permit, test the air, ventilate, post a standby

questions.stem: A welder working inside a tank finds the air stuffy and asks for the oxygen hose to be opened inside. Why must this never be done?
options: Oxygen is too costly to use for that purpose
Oxygen makes the welding arc unstable and hard to hold
Oxygen leaves a smell that stays in the tank
Extra oxygen makes clothing and grease burn fiercely

questions.stem: A hot work permit is issued for welding a bracket in a store room. When may the fire watch end?
options: Only after the time set on the permit, often 30–60 minutes
As soon as the welder strikes the last arc of the day
When the welder packs up and leaves the room
The next morning, when the store room is opened again

questions.stem: Before welding on a steel wall or partition, why must you check what is on the other side?
options: Heat passes through and can ignite hidden items
The paint on the far side makes the weld porous
The other side must be cooled with water first
Someone may need to hold the earth clamp there

questions.stem: An acetylene cylinder has been lying on its side in a truck. What should be done before it is used?
options: Shake it gently to mix the gas before it is used
Stand it upright and wait as the supplier says
Use it lying down so that the gas comes out faster
Open the valve fully to clear any liquid out first

questions.stem: What is the right way to check oxy-fuel hose connections for leaks?
options: Pass a lit match slowly along each connection
Brush on leak-test solution and look for bubbles
Smell each joint while the gas flows
Listen for a hiss at the torch valves

questions.stem: A welder must weld inside a damp steel tank. What is the main extra electrical risk?
options: A higher risk of electric shock
The arc will not strike on damp steel at all
The welding machine will use more electricity
The damp will make the electrodes burn faster

questions.stem: Before clearing a jam in a power guillotine, what must be done?
options: Isolate, lock and tag it, then check it cannot start
Switch it off at the start button and reach in quickly
Ask a co-worker to stand by the switch while you work
Keep it running slowly so the jam clears by itself

questions.stem: Three fitters will work on the same machine at the same time. How should it be locked off?
options: The supervisor fits one lock and keeps the key
Each fitter puts on their own lock, on a hasp
The first fitter fits a lock and the others trust it
A tag is enough, as all three know the machine is off

questions.stem: Which is the best sign that noise in the shop needs to be measured and controlled?
options: The machines can be heard over the shop radio
Visitors passing outside sometimes mention it
The noise stops for lunch and at the end of the shift
You must shout to be heard at about 1 m

questions.stem: Why is hearing damage from noise so serious?
options: It always causes pain, so workers stop work early
It heals within a few days once the noise stops
It builds slowly and cannot be cured or reversed
It only affects people who are over 50 years old

questions.stem: When ventilation alone does not keep welding fume away, which respiratory protection is suitable?
options: A cotton cloth tied over the nose and mouth
A particle respirator rated for welding fume, worn so it seals well on the face
A thin paper dust mask of the kind used for sanding
A gas-only cartridge with no particle filter

questions.stem: Why should a supervisor check that each worker's respirator fits?
options: A loose fit makes the filter wear out faster
A respirator works best on a worker with a full beard
Fume leaks in round the edges if the seal is poor
A tight fit stops the worker from talking

questions.stem: A 2 m × 1 m sheet of 10 mm steel plate weighs about 160 kg. What is the best way to move it?
options: Two strong trainees carry it, one at each end
Slide it across the floor by hand to the bench
One person lifts it with bent knees
Use a lifting aid such as a plate trolley or crane

questions.stem: Before using a chain sling, what should you check?
options: It is long enough to wrap twice round the whole load
It has been oiled within the last week
Its load tag, and its links and hooks for damage
It is the newest sling in the store

questions.stem: Which is the safest way to weld a bracket 4 m up a wall?
options: From the top step of a ladder, held by a co-worker
Standing on an empty drum placed on a bench
From a ladder, with one arm hooked round a rung
From a work platform with guardrails

questions.stem: Which extinguisher should NOT be used on a fire in an oil drum?
options: A foam extinguisher
A dry powder extinguisher
A carbon dioxide (CO2) extinguisher
A water jet extinguisher

questions.stem: Which is the best way to put out a small fire in a bin of cotton rags, away from any electrical equipment?
options: Carbon dioxide (CO2), which leaves no residue
Water or foam, which cools the burning cloth
None; let it burn out while someone watches
A damp rag flapped over the flames

questions.stem: Why should an emergency plan name wardens to check each area during an evacuation?
options: So every area is checked and nobody is left behind
So that the wardens can collect everyone's tools first
So workers can stay inside until a warden arrives
So the fire brigade does not need to be called

questions.stem: A welder gets a splash of pickling acid in one eye. What should be done first, before getting medical help?
options: Rub the eye gently with a clean cloth to remove the acid
Put in some eye drops from the first aid kit and rest
Rinse it at the eyewash for 15 minutes or more
Cover the eye with a dry pad and wait for it to settle

questions.stem: A welder has a large burn on the forearm from molten metal. Which is correct first aid while medical help is called?
options: Put butter or toothpaste on it to soothe it
Cool it with water, then cover it loosely
Burst the blisters so that the heat can escape
Pull off any cloth that is stuck to the burn

questions.stem: During hot weather in Spanish Town, a welder becomes confused and his skin is hot and dry. What should you do?
options: Call for medical help, move him to shade and cool him
Give him a sweet drink and send him back to the job soon
Let him sleep it off in the back of the company van
Tell him to finish the weld and then have a rest

questions.stem: When investigating an accident, who should be interviewed, and when?
options: Only the injured person, once they are back at work again
Witnesses and the injured person, as soon as possible
Only the supervisor, at the end of the month
Nobody, as the photos tell the whole story

questions.stem: A disc burst on a grinder and cut a worker's arm. Which of these is a root cause, rather than the immediate cause?
options: The disc broke into pieces while it was spinning
The worker's arm was cut by a flying piece
No system to check discs and guards
The worker was standing at the bench

questions.stem: Your team has had three near misses with unchained gas cylinders this month. What should the supervisor do?
options: Warn the team that the next person will be sacked
Wait for a real accident before changing anything
Find the cause, fix it, and brief the team
Remove the near miss forms so the record looks better

questions.stem: What makes a workplace safety inspection useful?
options: Doing it quickly, with no notes
Doing it only after an accident has happened
Checking only the areas that look untidy
A checklist, and actions that are followed up

questions.stem: A trainee keeps lifting his helmet to see the joint just as he strikes the arc. What should you do?
options: Let him carry on, as it only lasts a moment
Give him a darker filter so the arc is less bright
Tell him off in front of the class and move on
Stop him and coach him to set up first

questions.stem: A new primer arrives at the shop without a safety data sheet (SDS). What should you do?
options: Use it, as the label on the tin is enough
Use it outside, where the fumes will blow away
Get the SDS from the supplier and read it first
Mix a little with a primer you already know, to test it

questions.stem: Why should full oxygen cylinders be stored apart from fuel gas cylinders?
options: Oxygen cylinders are heavier and could crush them
The gases can mix through the cylinder walls
If a fire starts, oxygen makes it far fiercer
Fuel gas makes oxygen cylinders rust faster

questions.stem: You smell acetylene near the cylinder trolley. What should you do first?
options: Kill any flames, shut the valve if safe, ventilate
Light a match to find where the leak is coming from
Carry on working and report it at the end of the day
Spray water over the cylinders to cool them down

questions.stem: Why should hot slag and offcuts be cleared from a welding area during the shift, not only at the end?
options: They cause trips and burns, and can start fires
They make the welding machine run too hot
They change the colour of the welds
They make the earth clamp lose its grip

questions.stem: A welding machine's input lead is found to be cut through its outer sheath. What should the supervisor do?
options: Wrap it with tape and let the welder carry on
Use it only for small jobs until the end of the week
Isolate it, tag it out, and have it repaired
Ask the welder to keep the cut part off the floor

questions.stem: A welder refuses to cut open a drum that held fuel, because it has not been cleaned. What should the supervisor do?
options: Back the refusal, and have the drum made safe first
Tell the welder to cut it quickly near an open door
Find another welder who is willing to cut it
Fill the drum with oxygen to clear the fumes

questions.stem: Which of these shows a good safety culture in a fabrication shop?
options: Safety rules are followed only when the manager is there
Workers report hazards freely, and they are acted on
Near misses are kept quiet to keep the record clean
New trainees learn safety only by watching others

questions.stem: A contractor arrives to repair the shop's overhead crane. What should happen before they start?
options: Sign them in and give a site induction
Nothing, as contractors know their own work
They should start at once to save time
They should be given a free hand anywhere on site

questions.stem: Why should the work clamp (earth clamp) be fixed as close to the weld as possible?
options: So that the cable is long enough to reach the bench
So that the arc becomes brighter and easier to see
To stop welding current straying through other paths
So that the clamp itself stays cooler during long welds

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do we call the risk that is left after all the controls are in place?
In fume control, what do the letters LEV stand for?
What is the name of the illness, with fever, chills and a metal taste, caused by breathing zinc fume from galvanised steel?
What is the name of the very toxic gas that can form when the arc's light acts on chlorinated solvent vapour?
What device, fitted at the regulator or the torch, stops a flame travelling back into the hose and cylinder?
What do we call the person posted to look out for fires during and after hot work?
In a risk matrix, likelihood is multiplied by what, to give the risk score?
What do we call a space with limited ways in and out, such as a tank or a pit, where bad air can build up?
What is the name of the device, fitted to some welding machines, that lowers the open-circuit voltage when the welder is not welding?
What is the name of the method of locking and tagging an isolator so that a machine cannot be switched on during work?
Inside an acetylene cylinder, the acetylene is dissolved in which liquid?
What do we call the underlying reason an incident happened, which must be fixed to stop it happening again?
What do the letters RPE stand for?
What is the name of the written approval needed before anyone enters a confined space?
What is the name of the most serious heat illness, in which the body can no longer cool itself and the person may become confused?

essays.stem: Using a risk matrix, explain how you would assess and control the risks of fitting and welding a steel gate at a customer's house.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would visit the site, or get photos, and list each step of the job: unloading, setting out, fixing the posts, welding the hinges, grinding and painting. For each step I would list the hazards, such as arc flash to the family and people passing, fire from dry grass, electric shock from a generator lead, handling the heavy gate, and grinding sparks. For each hazard I would score the likelihood and the severity from 1 to 5 and multiply them, so a likely (4) and serious (4) burn risk scores 16, which is high. Then I would choose controls in order: remove the hazard where I can, for example by welding most of the gate in the shop; then engineering controls such as screens and guards; then rules such as a hot work permit, a fire watch and keeping people back; and last, PPE. I would score the risk again to check it is now acceptable, record it all, brief the team, and review it if conditions change on the day.
markingPoints: Breaks the job into steps and lists the hazards of each step
Scores each hazard for likelihood and severity and works out the risk score
Chooses controls in the right order: eliminate, substitute, engineering, administrative, PPE
Gives job-specific controls, such as shop welding, screens, permit and fire watch
Re-scores the residual risk, records it, briefs the team and reviews it

essays.stem: Describe how to plan and control hot work outside the welding shop, from the permit to the end of the fire watch.
essays.modelAnswer: Hot work outside the welding shop needs a permit from the person in charge. Before work starts, the area is inspected. Anything that can burn is moved away, often 10 m or more, or covered with fire-resisting blankets, and gaps in floors and walls are sealed so that sparks cannot fall through. The far side of walls and partitions is checked. Drums and pipes that held fuel must not be welded until they are made safe. A suitable extinguisher and a fire blanket are placed at hand, and screens are set up to protect other people from arc flash. The permit records the job, the place, the time, the precautions, and the names of the welder and the fire watch. A trained fire watch stays during the work and for the time the permit sets after it finishes, often 30 to 60 minutes, checking for smouldering. At the end, the area is inspected again, and the permit is signed off and returned.
markingPoints: A permit is issued by the person in charge before work starts
Combustibles are removed or covered, gaps sealed, and the far side of walls checked
Extinguisher, fire blanket and screens are in place before work starts
A fire watch stays during the work and for the set time afterwards
The area is checked at the end and the permit is signed off

essays.stem: Explain the health risks of welding fume, and describe how a supervisor should control them when welding mild steel, galvanised steel and stainless steel.
essays.modelAnswer: Welding fume is a mix of very fine metal particles and gases. Breathing it can cause coughing, lung disease and, over many years, some cancers. The arc can also produce gases such as ozone and carbon monoxide. For mild steel, the main controls are local exhaust ventilation close to the arc, good general ventilation, keeping the head out of the plume, and a fume-rated respirator if extraction is not enough. Galvanised steel gives off zinc fume, which can cause metal fume fever, so the zinc should be removed from the weld area first where the procedure allows, and extraction must be used. Stainless steel fume contains chromium and nickel compounds that can cause cancer, so extraction at the source is essential, and suitable respirators are often needed too. The supervisor should check that the extraction works, that respirators fit and are kept clean, and that welders are trained. The SDS for each filler and the Centre's rules must be followed.
markingPoints: Fume is fine particles and gases that can harm the lungs and cause long-term illness
Mild steel: extraction at the arc, ventilation, head out of the plume, respirator if needed
Galvanised: zinc fume and metal fume fever; remove the coating where allowed and extract
Stainless: chromium and nickel compounds; extraction essential, respirators often needed
Supervisor checks extraction, respirator fit and training, and follows the SDS

essays.stem: Describe the precautions for safe entry and welding inside a confined space, such as a water tank.
essays.modelAnswer: First, ask whether the work can be done from outside, so that nobody needs to go in. If entry is needed, it must be planned and a confined space entry permit issued. The tank is isolated: pipes are blanked or disconnected, and pumps and power are locked off. It is cleaned if needed, and the air is tested by a trained person with a gas detector for oxygen, flammable gas and toxic gas, before entry and during the work. Fresh air is blown in with a fan; oxygen must never be used to freshen the air. Gas cylinders stay outside, and hoses and torches are taken out at breaks. The welder wears suitable PPE, uses dry gloves and an insulating mat, and the welding machine is set up as the maker says for damp or cramped places. A trained standby person stays at the entry the whole time, keeps in contact, and has a rescue plan and equipment ready. The permit is closed when everyone is out.
markingPoints: Avoid entry if possible; otherwise plan it and issue an entry permit
Isolate the tank and test the air before and during the work
Ventilate with fresh air, never oxygen; keep cylinders outside
Electrical precautions: dry gloves, insulating mat, suitable machine set-up
A standby person at the entry with a rescue plan; permit closed at the end

essays.stem: A trainee was cut when a grinding disc burst. Describe how you would investigate the accident and what your report would include.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would make the area safe, make sure the trainee gets first aid and medical help, and leave the scene as it is as far as is safe. I would report the accident to the supervisor and the person in charge of safety. Then I would collect evidence: photos of the grinder, the pieces of the disc and the guard, the markings on the disc such as its size and maximum speed, and the grinder's speed. I would interview the trainee and any witnesses, one at a time and as soon as possible, using open questions. I would look for the immediate cause, such as a disc rated below the grinder's speed or a missing guard, and the root causes, such as no checks on discs, the wrong discs in stock, or poor training. My report would give the date, time and place, the people involved, what happened in order, the injury, the causes, and the actions to stop it happening again, with names and dates. I would follow up to check that the actions were done.
markingPoints: Makes the area safe, gives first aid, keeps the scene and reports it
Collects evidence: photos, disc markings and grinder details
Interviews the injured person and witnesses promptly with open questions
Finds both the immediate cause and the root causes
Report covers the facts in order, causes, and actions with names and dates, then follows up

essays.stem: Describe how to store, move and use oxygen and acetylene cylinders safely, and what to do if a leak or a flashback happens.
essays.modelAnswer: Cylinders are stored upright and chained or secured, in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place away from heat, sparks and oil. Oxygen is kept apart from fuel gases such as acetylene, by distance or a fire-resisting wall, as the rules say. Full and empty cylinders are kept apart and labelled, and valve caps are fitted when cylinders are not in use. They are moved on a proper trolley, never rolled on their sides or lifted by the valve. Acetylene cylinders must stay upright, and one that has been lying down should stand for the time the supplier gives before use. In use, regulators and flashback arrestors are fitted, connections are tested with leak-test solution, and oil and grease are kept away from oxygen fittings. If a leak is found, flames are put out, the cylinder valve is closed if it is safe, the area is ventilated and people are kept away. If a flashback happens, the valves are closed in the order the maker and the Centre's rules give, and the equipment is checked before it is used again.
markingPoints: Stored upright and secured, ventilated, away from heat and oil, oxygen apart from fuel gas
Moved on a trolley with caps on; acetylene kept upright
Regulators and flashback arrestors fitted; leak test with solution; no oil on oxygen fittings
Leak: flames out, valve closed if safe, ventilate, keep people away
Flashback: valves closed in the order the maker and the Centre give; equipment checked

essays.stem: Explain how you, as a team leader, would carry out a workplace safety inspection and make sure that the faults found are fixed.
essays.modelAnswer: I would plan the inspection with a checklist made for our shop, covering walkways and exits, housekeeping, machine guards, power leads and welding cables, gas cylinders, extraction and ventilation, fire equipment, first aid, PPE, chemicals and SDSs, and signs. I would choose a time when work is going on, so I can see real practice, and take another team member with me. I would walk the whole area, look and ask questions, write down each fault and where it is, and take photos. For each fault I would judge how serious it is. Anything dangerous, such as a damaged lead, would be dealt with at once by taking it out of use. The findings would go on an action list, saying what must be done, who will do it and by when. I would report to the manager, share the results with the team, check later that each action was completed, and then sign it off.
markingPoints: Uses a checklist that covers the main hazards of the shop
Inspects while work is going on, records each fault, its place and photos
Judges how serious each fault is and deals with dangerous ones at once
Makes an action list with what, who and by when
Reports, shares the results, and checks that actions are completed

essays.stem: Describe the electrical hazards of arc welding and how to control them, especially in hot, damp conditions.
essays.modelAnswer: Arc welding uses a high current, and the open-circuit voltage of the machine can give a shock, especially when the welder's body is wet with sweat, the gloves are damp, or the welder is in contact with steel. In Jamaica's heat this risk is greater. Controls start with the machine: it should be inspected, correctly earthed on its supply side, fed from a protected supply, and repaired only by a competent person. Cables, the electrode holder and the work clamp must be in good condition with no bare parts, and the work clamp should be fixed close to the weld. The welder should wear dry leather gloves and dry clothing, change gloves when they get wet, stand on a dry insulating mat in damp places, and never change an electrode with bare hands. In tanks or other damp, cramped places, a machine with a voltage-reducing device, or a DC supply, is often used as the procedure says. The supply is isolated before any repair.
markingPoints: Explains shock risk from open-circuit voltage, made worse by sweat, damp and contact with steel
Machine inspected, supply side earthed and protected, repaired only by a competent person
Cables, holder and clamp in good condition; clamp close to the weld
Dry gloves and clothing, insulating mat, never bare hands on the electrode
Extra measures in damp places (for example a voltage-reducing device) and isolation before repair

essays.stem: Explain how a supervisor can build a good safety culture in a fabrication team. Give practical examples.
essays.modelAnswer: A good safety culture means everyone treats safety as part of doing the job well, even when no one is watching. The supervisor sets the example by always wearing PPE and following the rules. He or she makes it easy to report hazards and near misses, thanks people who report, and acts quickly, so that workers see that reports matter. Blame is avoided when things go wrong, so that people tell the truth and causes can be found. Regular toolbox talks keep safety in mind, and workers are asked for their ideas on making jobs safer. New trainees get a proper induction and are watched and coached until they work safely. Good work is praised, and unsafe acts are stopped and corrected calmly. Safety figures, such as near misses reported and actions closed, can be posted on the notice board. Workers are allowed to stop a job they believe is unsafe, and they are backed when they do.
markingPoints: Explains what a safety culture is
Supervisor sets the example with PPE and rules
Encourages reporting, avoids blame and acts on reports quickly
Uses toolbox talks, consultation, induction and coaching
Allows workers to stop unsafe work and backs them

essays.stem: Describe how to plan a lift of a heavy steel fabrication using a crane or chain block, including the checks on the lifting gear.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would find the weight of the load from the drawing or by working it out, and where its centre of gravity is. I would choose lifting equipment, such as an overhead crane, a gantry with a chain block, or a forklift, with a safe working load greater than the load plus the slings. I would check that the crane or block, the slings and the shackles have a current inspection tag, show their safe working load, and have no damage such as stretched links, cut fibres or bent hooks. I would plan the route, the landing place and the blocks to set the load on, and keep people clear of the area. One trained person would give the signals. The load is lifted a little first and checked for balance, then moved slowly, with tag lines to control any swing. Nobody stands under a hanging load. After the lift, the gear is checked and stored, and any damage is reported.
markingPoints: Finds the weight and centre of gravity of the load
Chooses equipment with a safe working load greater than the load and slings
Checks tags and condition of the crane or block, slings and shackles
Plans the route and landing, keeps people clear, one signaller
Test lift, slow movement with tag lines, no one under the load; gear checked after

practical1.title: Job safety analysis, hot work permit and site set-up for a welding job outside the welding shop
practical1.brief: As a group, plan and set up the safety controls for a hot work job outside the welding shop, as a team leader would before work starts. The assessor names a place at the Centre (for example, fitting a new steel bracket to a column in the store room or an outdoor shed) and gives the group a blank job safety analysis (JSA) form, a risk matrix and a hot work permit. No welding is done. Stage 1, survey: walk the area together, and note and photograph the hazards (things that can burn, gaps where sparks could fall, people passing, the power supply, ventilation and access at height). Stage 2, paperwork: break the job into steps on the JSA, score each hazard with the risk matrix, choose controls in the right order, and score the risk that is left. Fill in the hot work permit for the assessor to check and sign. Stage 3, set-up: put the controls in place: move or cover anything that can burn, set up screens, place a suitable extinguisher and fire blanket, put up signs and barriers, and plan the fire watch. Stage 4: one member gives a 5-minute toolbox talk on the job's hazards and controls, and every member signs the JSA. Each member leads at least one stage or one part of the paperwork. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Then return the area to normal.
materials: Blank JSA forms and a risk matrix (from the assessor)
Fire-resisting blankets for covering items that cannot be moved
A suitable fire extinguisher and a fire blanket
photos: The area before set-up, showing the hazards found
The completed JSA with the risk scores
The completed hot work permit, before the assessor signs it
Items that can burn moved away or covered, and gaps sealed
Screens, extinguisher, fire blanket, signs and barriers in place
The toolbox talk, and the JSA signed by every member
checklist: Found the main hazards in the area, including hidden ones such as the far side of a wall
Scored the risks with the matrix and chose controls in the right order
Completed the JSA and the hot work permit clearly and correctly
Set up the controls properly: items that can burn cleared or covered, screens, extinguisher, signs
Explained the fire watch: who, where and for how long, as the permit says
Led or took part in the toolbox talk and signed the JSA
Worked safely and returned the area to normal
safety: No welding, cutting or grinding is done in this practical
Wear safety boots and gloves when moving screens and stores
Lift heavy items together or with a trolley, and never block exits or fire equipment
Do not climb without the right access equipment; follow the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Investigate a staged workplace incident and write the incident report
practical2.brief: As a group, investigate a staged incident and report on it, as a supervisor would. Before the group arrives, the assessor sets up a scene in the workshop with the power isolated: for example, a member playing an injured trainee beside a bench grinder with its guard removed and a broken disc on the floor, a welding lead lying across a walkway, and a gas cylinder standing unchained nearby. Nothing is live and no one is really hurt. Stage 1: make the scene safe (check that the power is isolated and tagged, and keep others back), and give first aid to the 'injured' member as practised: check for danger, call for help, and dress the 'wound' on the arm, wearing gloves. Stage 2: collect evidence: photograph the scene, measure and sketch where things are, note the markings on the disc, and interview the 'injured' member and two 'witnesses' played by members, one at a time. Stage 3: work out the immediate causes and the root causes. Stage 4: write the incident report: date, time, place, people, what happened in order, the injury and first aid given, the causes, and corrective actions with names and dates. Stage 5: present the findings to the assessor as if to the manager. Every member takes a role (first aider, photographer, interviewer, sketcher or report writer), and the group checks the report together. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and the report to the group's practical.
materials: A staged scene set up by the assessor, with the power isolated, locked off and tagged
First aid kit with dressings and disposable gloves
Incident report form and witness statement forms
Tape measure, clipboard, pens and plain paper for the sketch
photos: The scene as found, from at least two sides
The isolation and tag being checked
First aid being given to the 'injured' member
Close-ups of the evidence: the guard, the disc markings, the cable and the cylinder
The sketch of the scene with measurements
The finished incident report and action list
checklist: Made the scene safe before going near, and checked the isolation
Gave or helped with first aid correctly, wearing gloves
Collected evidence: photos, measurements, a sketch and the disc markings
Asked open, fair questions in the interviews and wrote statements accurately
Found both the immediate causes and the root causes
Wrote or checked a report that is factual, complete and in order
Proposed corrective actions with names and dates, and presented them clearly
safety: Everything in the scene is isolated, locked off and tagged by the assessor; nothing is switched on
The injury is pretend: use only clean dressings and wear disposable gloves
Do not handle the broken disc pieces with bare hands
Keep the walkway clear for other people, and follow the Centre's rules
